accepted_units.title: Convert local source data into a global cohomological obstruction
accepted_units.why_material: The source separates a sourced differential problem into an equation of motion and a Bianchi identity, then observes that local delta-function sources can be integrated into a global field only when their total class vanishes. After this existence gate, parity and a chosen trivial cohomology class remove the harmonic freedom and select a unique solution. The reusable move is to test a local source prescription first against the global quotient that annihilates exact data, then state the normalization that makes the solution canonical.
accepted_units.context_note: The cohomological neutrality condition and uniqueness claim are made within the source's eleven-dimensional supergravity set-up and stated perturbative order. Five-brane contributions extend the source class in the following unit. This is source-grounded conditional reasoning, not an unconditional theorem for arbitrary singular PDEs. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the normalized Bianchi formulas, coefficients, and parity notation are flattened and must be checked against the typeset source for exact use. Representation limit: the argument is expressed for differential forms with distributional sources, an involution, and a cohomology class constraint. Scope limit: vanishing total source class is necessary here and paired with a stated Hodge-type solution claim; it does not by itself guarantee analytic existence, regularity, boundary behavior, or uniqueness for arbitrary operators or singular spaces.

accepted_units.title: Admit a new source by matching the component type used by the solver
accepted_units.why_material: Rather than redoing the complete calculation after adding a new kind of singular source, the source decomposes forms into holomorphic, antiholomorphic, and transverse degrees and identifies the single component type on which the later computation depends. Placing the new source on compatible geometric data makes it contribute in that same type, so the established solution strategy survives. This is a reusable modularity test: determine which graded component an argument actually consumes and require extensions to land in that component.
accepted_units.context_note: The type-matching argument is conditional on holomorphic source curves and points in the interval/orbifold direction. The claim that five-branes cause no further difficulty is scoped to the computation described by the source. Novelty unconfirmed.

accepted_units.title: Solve a coupled system by integrability, Hodge choice, and kernel interpretation
accepted_units.why_material: The source first checks that the right-hand side of a differential equation is annihilated by the next differential. Hodge theory then supplies a common solution to the differential equation and gauge-like divergence condition at each parameter value, unique modulo a harmonic form. A final evolution equation fixes parameter dependence, leaving only a parameter-independent harmonic ambiguity, which is interpreted as motion in the background moduli. The reusable pattern cleanly separates consistency, existence, evolution, and semantic meaning of the kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly checks compatibility of the three equations using identities derived earlier and identifies the harmonic (1,1) freedom with Kahler-modulus displacement. This is within a compact Calabi-Yau and first-order perturbative calculation. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: the three displayed equations are substantially flattened; their exact signs and constants require typeset verification, while the prose statement of integrability and Hodge uniqueness is clear. Representation limit: the method depends on differential-form degree, a Hodge decomposition, a divergence condition, and an external interval parameter. Scope limit: compactness and the relevant Hodge theory are essential, and uniqueness is only modulo the harmonic kernel; on noncompact, singular, or boundary spaces the existence and kernel statement can change.

accepted_units.title: Bootstrap a metric-dependent system from a scalar potential in a reference metric
accepted_units.why_material: A field equation appears circular because its divergence operator depends on the unknown corrected metric. The source first solves the metric-independent source equation in a reference geometry by dualizing the field to the gradient of a scalar potential. Supersymmetry then forces the conformal correction to be a function of that same potential; consequently the corrected equation reduces to closure of a scalar function of the potential times its differential and is automatically compatible. The nonlinear fields and warp factors are thereby compressed to one sourced scalar problem plus algebraic functions of its solution.
accepted_units.context_note: The source presents this as an exact all-orders solution of the stated six-dimensional supergravity system, distinct from the earlier linearized four-dimensional analysis. Exactness is internal to that physical truncation and ansatz, not a general mathematical theorem about nonlinear metric-field systems. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: Hodge-dual, Laplacian, exponential, and conformal-factor formulas contain displaced notation; exact exponents and constants need the typeset source. Representation limit: the reduction uses a five-dimensional internal metric, a conformal ansatz, duality between a four-form and scalar gradient, and the supersymmetry equations. Scope limit: the bootstrap works because the correction depends only on the potential and because the Bianchi identity is metric-independent; a general metric-dependent PDE need not share either property.

accepted_units.title: Fix additive freedom at a boundary minimum and expose the positivity threshold
accepted_units.why_material: The scalar potential is determined only up to a constant. Because it is harmonic in the interior, the source uses the maximum principle to place its minimum on the boundary, fixes the additive ambiguity by setting that minimum to zero, and then reads regularity of the reconstructed metric from positivity of a single shifted factor. This is a reusable move: normalize a kernel freedom at an extremal locus so that loss of admissibility becomes a transparent threshold condition.
accepted_units.context_note: The minimum argument allows singular positive sources and is applied on the orbifold interval with boundary. The resulting metric singularity is a conclusion of the source's supergravity solution; its physical interpretation is treated cautiously by the source. Novelty unconfirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extraction limit: this passage is prose-readable, but the exact conformal factor is inherited from damaged displayed equations in the previous unit. Representation limit: the normalization uses a scalar harmonic potential, an additive-constant kernel, a boundary, and reconstruction through a positive conformal factor. Scope limit: the maximum principle requires its usual ellipticity and domain hypotheses, and interior singularities, sign-changing sources, noncompactness, or different boundary conditions can change where extrema occur and what the threshold means.
